title: Distinct triangle areas in the triangular grid
statement: In the triangular grid T_n (the points a + b e^(i pi/3) with integers a, b >= 0 and a + b <= n - 1), the area of a triangle with vertices in T_n is an integer multiple |da1 db2 - da2 db1| of the unit triangle's area sqrt(3)/4. Let t(n) be the largest number of points of T_n such that every three of them span a triangle of nonzero area and all these C(t,3) areas are different. Determine t(n); the headline cell is n = 30: find 10 or more points of T_30 with all triangle areas distinct and nonzero.
submission: Text file: one point per line, 'a b' with a, b >= 0 and a + b <= 29.
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: 9 points of T_30 with distinct nonzero triangle areas, found by randomized greedy construction with local search (tools/tri_distinct_search.py, mode areas)

context: Erdos and Purdy asked how many distinct areas the triangles of n points must span; the grid version, choosing as many grid points as possible with all triangle areas different, is a two-dimensional relative of Sidon sets (all sums different) and Golomb rulers, and its square-grid form appears in the OEIS (A322740, smallest rectangle containing n points with distinct triangle areas). In the triangular grid areas are measured in units of the unit triangle and are the absolute values of 2 x 2 determinants of lattice vectors, so the problem asks for point sets whose determinant triples never repeat; with all areas at most (n - 1)^2, C(t,3) <= (n - 1)^2 gives t(n) = O(n^(2/3)), and how close the truth is to that bound is open.
references: P. Brass, W. Moser, J. Pach, Research Problems in Discrete Geometry (Springer, 2005): problems of Erdos and Purdy on distinct areas
OEIS A322740 (the square-grid relative: least rectangle area from which n points with distinct triangle areas can be chosen)

novelty.verdict: new. The sequence t(n) is not in the OEIS and no paper on distinct triangle areas in the triangular grid was found; the square-grid question in A322740 is the closest.
closest: OEIS A322740: least area of a grid rectangle containing n points whose triangles all have distinct areas (square grid; a different objective on a different lattice).

first_values.note: Exact values by exhaustive search over subsets of T_n (tools/src/trigrid.c areas); n = 30 is our best known lower bound.

baseline.text: 9 for n = 30, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the points in `refs/tri-areas.txt`. Upper bound: the C(t,3) areas are distinct integers between 1 and 29^2 = 841, so C(t,3) <= 841 and t(30) <= 18.

bound.source: C(t,3) <= 841 distinct nonzero areas (in units of sqrt(3)/4)
